overall: At 2:09 AM ET on the summer solstice, Atlanta is holding at 73.4°F — notably warmer than the NWS-forecast overnight low of ~69°F — with temperatures completely flat (velocity +0.0°F/hr) as expected in the pre-dawn hours. Cloud cover is moderate (~62%) with a few-cloud sky designation and a very humid dewpoint of 69.8°F, suggesting a moist airmass in place. No active alerts and the NWS calls for mostly sunny skies today, which is supportive of significant daytime heating.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show tight agreement on the TMAX range — ECMWF 86.3°F, NBM 86.4°F, and HRRR 84.6°F all cluster in the 84–87°F band — while the NWS narrative forecasts a high near 89°F, creating a modest but meaningful gap of ~2–4°F between the numerical models and the official forecast. Peak timing consensus is strong (16–17h ET, spread only 0.5 hours), lending confidence to the afternoon timing but not the magnitude.
max_temp_prediction: The META probability distribution (most reliable model) concentrates ~73% of probability in the 86–91°F range, with the 86–87°F and 88–89°F buckets tied at 28.6% each, yielding a META-weighted expected TMAX of approximately 87.5–88°F. Summer solstice solar insolation and mostly sunny skies support reaching the upper end of the NWP envelope, but the NWP consensus (~85.8°F average) tempers the NWS 89°F call; confidence is moderate given Tier 4 ensemble signals indicating meaningful spread. Best estimate is 87.5°F with a likely range of 85–90°F.
